Reading time travels with the brief

Terminal Delight’s native reader now records visible time and saves it beside your notes in the HTML. The test build works; your running Terminal Delight has not been replaced.

01 The counter follows the page

Still and active counts. Another pane, tab, window or note dialog pauses it. FOCUS, zoom and resize keep the same clock. Unknown time stays unknown; interrupted monitoring leaves a gap.

02 Both readers keep one history

Copy map and native send-back include anchored time. Failed saves remain pending for retry. A quick pass is exposure data; it still needs interpretation.

Implementation choices

Judgement calls

Nobody had decided these, so I did and kept working. Stamp the ones you agree with.

Keep the browser origin stable

Chose
Remember one loopback port per file; rotate the access token on restart.
Because
Pending browser checkpoints live under their origin. A new port would leave them unreachable after restarting the review server.

Meanwhile: carrying on as if you concur.

Build the native reader on the current preview

Chose
Use an isolated feature branch from the current T3 preview, with its matching private renderer.
Because
The current preview contains the newer HTML open path; starting from the older integration branch would omit that working code. Release assignment remains unassigned.

Meanwhile: carrying on as if you concur.
